To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed chiral nematic photonic microspheres that can be assembled into organized superstructures that communicate light in a wavelength and chirality selective manner, and that can be reversibly switched by the use of photoresponsive dopants.

(i) chiral nematic colloidal spheres can communicate optically with each other and (ii) the wavelength, polarization, and direction of the optical communication can be tuned by doping the microspheres with photoresponsive molecules.
we have designed and synthesized chiral nematic colloids whose shape enables them, when assembled in superstructures, to reflect light of specific wavelength and handedness in any direction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new functional materials, which can be used as all-optical distributors of light and as all-optical switches, which can be tuned in a controlled way by external stimuli, e.g. light, heat, magnetic field, etc.
the design, synthesis and application of chiral molecular switches and their self-assembly into organized structures.
the design, preparation and study of new functional materials that can be applied in photonics and optoelectronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a novel type of chiral nematics with a unique shape and size that can be assembled in superstructures with high selectivity.

we have designed and demonstrated that chiral nematic liquid crystal microspheres, when organized in superstructures, are able to reflect light in all directions and that their chiroptically selective communication can be switched by light.

this study demonstrates the potential of a new generation of chiral nematics, in particular, chiral nematic liquid crystals (CNLCs), for the development of new optical devices, in which the wavelength and the handedness of light can be controlled by external stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed a new material that can reflect light of different wavelength and chirality in all directions and that we have demonstrated how this material can be switched between these two states of reflection.
we have demonstrated that chiral nematic colloids can be used to control the direction of light and its chirality, and that the chiroptical properties of the colloids can be switched by light.

we developed a new class of photonic materials, whose shape, size and composition allow them to reflect light in all directions and to communicate optically in a selective way, and which can be reversibly switched between different states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chiroptical properties of the microspheres, their size and their arrangement can be used to design and control light transmission, distribution, and switching.

the chiroptical response of the superstructures is determined by the shape of their building blocks and by the interplay between the optical properties of the microspheres and of the photo-responsive dopants.
the combination of chiroptical and all-optical properties in a single material can be exploited to design and develop advanced optical communication devices.
